title: Grandparents and a step-grandfather who laid telephone wire out west
summary: Raised by his father's parents; his mother's father, a Webb sea captain, was lost at sea and her mother remarried Charles Weaver, who left him the revolver that began his gun collecting.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh huh. And you were raised by your grandparents. Your mother separated from your father and then your grandparents took over, right?

Well, my father worked in the trucking business as a subsidiary of my grandfather. Well, he did very well; he got his own job in a wholesale trucking business. My grandfather had his own business. Now when

they separated, my father went into the war and my mother pursuing her career, thought that rather than take me with her, because she went to Boston with the Conservatory, one of the org & 16, the big console? She thought I would be better off, she thought, with my grandfolks who were set up. They were just middle down the road people, you know.
Did we mention your grandparents' name?
No. My grandfather's name was John Gilmore.
Your grandfather? How about your grandmother?
My grandmother's name was Annie -- I think she used the name Annie, and I forget her middle name.
Now which grandparents were they? Were they your mother's or your father's?
These were my father's.
Your father's parents. And what about your mother's parents?
My mother's parents -- my great grandfather, no it would be my grandfather on my mother's side -- her mother's husband was lost at sea, he was a sea captain. He was a Webb.
Oh, that was his name? Webb?
Yes, That's where my mother got the name Webb.
Oh, I see.

And he was lost at sea. Then her mother married a very colorful person -- where I got the name Spencer, and his name was -- oh, I have it all, but it's an awful lot to recall at once. But he laid telephone wires out through the Middle West.
Who was that that laid the telephone wires out to the Middle West?
My grandfather, I guess what you would call my step-grandfather. My grandmother's on my mother's side, second husband.
Uh huh. How did he get out to the midwest? He was from Portland, Maine.
His name was Charles Weaver.
Charles Weaver was his name?
Yes, and he laid the telephone wires in the wild and wooly west during the 1800's.
You know, that's a long way from Portland, Maine. Do you have any idea how he got out there?

He went out with the telephone company. Now how he went there as a young man to make his reputation with the company, I suppose. But he became an executive after he returned. I know, becase that's what got me into guns -- he left me a revolver that he carried to the west, and that's what started me collecting.
Oh, we'll get into that.
We'll get into it later on. But that was his background.
